dosing_regimen.source_excerpt: protocolSection.armsInterventionsModule interventions and armGroups: "Placebo" "Starting at Week 16, all participants received open-label risankizumab 150 mg subcutaneous injections once every 12 weeks (q12w) at Weeks 16, 28, and 40." "Drug: Placebo for Risankizumab" "Drug: Risankizumab" "Risankizumab" "Participants received risankizumab 150 mg subcutaneous injections during the 16-week Double-blind Period at Baseline (Day 1) and Week 4." "Starting at Week 16, all participants received open-label risankizumab 150 mg subcutaneous injections once every 12 weeks (q12w) at Weeks 16, 28, and 40." "Drug: Risankizumab" "Placebo for Risankizumab" "Subcutaneous (SC) Injection" "Placebo" "Risankizumab" "Subcutaneous (SC) Injection" "Placebo" "Risankizumab" -- CT.gov intervention descriptions are copied verbatim. The registry links Risankizumab to both randomized arm labels because placebo participants cross to open-label risankizumab from Week 16. Initial dosing is at Baseline (Day 1) and Week 4; active dosing then occurs q12w at Weeks 16, 28, and 40. q12w has no matching frequency enum, so frequency remains null. Periods record stated administration dates, not an inferred number of doses.

prohibited_concomitant: During the study, no biologic treatment is allowed, apart from commercially available risankizumab after the Week 52 or Premature Discontinuation assessments when deemed appropriate by the investigator and subject.
Systemic non-biologic therapies used to treat psoriasis, including cyclosporine, corticosteroids, methotrexate, retinoids, apremilast, and fumaric acid derivatives, are prohibited.
Phototherapy (UVB, UVA including PUVA), laser therapy, tanning booths, and extended sun exposure that could affect disease severity or interfere with assessments are prohibited.

Topical psoriasis treatments, including corticosteroids, anthralin, calcipotriene, topical vitamin D derivatives, retinoids, urea, alpha- or beta-hydroxyl acids, and medicated shampoos, are prohibited.
permitted_concomitant: Stable doses of concomitant therapies for chronic conditions are permissible when neither the condition nor treatment is judged to exclude the participant.

Moisturizers without active ingredients used for at least 2 weeks before Baseline and expected to continue through Week 16 are allowed; subjects should not apply emollients within 8 hours before study assessments.
Only inhaled, topical ophthalmic, or intranasal corticosteroids are permitted during the study.
Non-live vaccines may be administered during screening or treatment if not contraindicated or medically inappropriate.
value.population_note: This is a risankizumab versus placebo trial with prohibited and permitted concomitant therapies. The protocol does not specify a standardized background psoriasis regimen; do not infer monotherapy from the assigned arms.

background_therapy.source_excerpt: 5.3 Prohibited Medications and Therapy; 5.4 Prior and Concomitant Therapy; 4.1 Overall Study Design and Plan: "This is a Phase 3b multicenter, randomized, double-blind, parallel-group, placebo-controlled study to" "evaluate the safety and efficacy of risankizumab (150 mg) compared to placebo in adult subjects with" "During the study, no biologic treatment is allowed." "Exception: Treatment with commercially" "available risankizumab after the Week 52/Premature Discontinuation (PD) assessments if this" "has been determined as an appropriate subsequent treatment by the investigator in discussion" "with the subject." "Systemic (including oral or injectable administrations) non-biologic therapy that can be used to" "treat PsO, including but not limited to cyclosporine, corticosteroids, methotrexate, retinoids," "apremilast, and fumaric acid derivatives." "Phototherapy treatment (UVB or ultraviolet A [UVA] phototherapy, including PUVA), laser" "therapy, tanning booth, or extended sun exposure that could affect disease severity or interfere" "with disease assessments." "Topical PsO treatments, including but not limited to corticosteroids, anthralin, calcipotriene," "topical vitamin D derivatives, retinoids, urea, α- or β-hydroxyl acids, and medicated shampoos" "(for example those that contain corticosteroids, coal tar, or vitamin D3 analogues)." "Non-live vaccines may be administered during screening or treatment period, if not contraindicated or" " Moisturizers: Provided that moisturizers (without active ingredients) have been used for at least" "2 weeks prior to Baseline and are anticipated to be continuously used at least until the Week 16" "visit." "Subjects should not apply emollients within 8 hours prior to study assessments." " Only inhaled, topical ophthalmic, or intranasal corticosteroids are permitted during the study." -- Medication restrictions apply during the study, while the exception allows commercially available risankizumab after Week 52 or premature discontinuation as a subsequent treatment. Prior prohibited-medication washout is not represented as a treatment-period prohibition. The source states stable chronic-condition therapies and the listed moisturizer and corticosteroid uses are allowed.

multiplicity_control.source_excerpt: SAP Sections 9.3, 9.4.2, and 13.0: "The primary efficacy endpoint is the achievement of ppIGA of 0 or 1 with at least a" "2-point reduction from Baseline at Week 16 as defined in Section 3.1." "a two-sided significance level of 0.05:" "The following null hypotheses pertaining to the ranked secondary efficacy endpoints will" "All statistical tests" "will be performed at a 2-sided alpha level of 0.05." "be tested between the risankizumab and placebo groups among the ITT Population in a" "hierarchical order, only if the null hypothesis for the primary endpoint has been rejected:" "There is no difference between risankizumab and placebo, with respect to the" "proportion of subjects achieving PPASI 75 at Week 16" "There is no difference between risankizumab and placebo, with respect to the" "proportion of subjects achieving PPASI 90 at Week 16" "There is no difference between risankizumab and placebo, with respect to the" "proportion of subjects achieving sPGA of" "clear" "or" "almost clear" "(0 or 1) with at" "least a 2-point reduction from Baseline at Week 16" "There is no difference between risankizumab and placebo, with respect to the" "proportion of subjects achieving PPASI 100 at Week 16" "Overall type-I error will be controlled by testing the primary efficacy endpoint, followed" "by the ranked secondary efficacy endpoints, in a hierarchical order as described in" "Section 9.3 and Section 9.4." -- The SAP states the primary endpoint and the four ranked secondary endpoints, tests the secondary endpoints in hierarchical order after rejection of the primary null, and explicitly states overall Type-I error control. This is represented as serial gatekeeping at two-sided 0.05. SAP version 3.0 is cited for the plan; finalization status is not separately asserted.
